page.overview:
What is Vorvadoss?

Vorvadoss (also known as The Flaming One) is a fictional deity in the Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Henry Kuttner for his short story "The Eater of Souls".

Cloaked in a silvery mist of darkness, only inklings of the face of the entity have ever been visible, described as utterly inhuman and only half-visible features arranged in non-human patterns following alien geometries. Its eyes are clear and black, with tiny green flickering flames seen within them. If inclined to help, despite its passionless alien expression, it can induce reassurance in one who beholds it. (: "The Invaders," Henry Kuttner)

The only known worshippers dwell on Bel Yarnak, the inhabitants of which are only known to be non-anthropoid and utterly unlike mankind in countenance. Vorvadoss has forbidden its own worship to any but the Sindara, the rulers of Bel Yarnak, whom can call upon the deity for advice. Vorvadoss seems to respond in - perhaps manipulative - riddles, as suits its purposes. In fact, it said that "Thou goest to doom, but thy son sleeps in Bel Yarnak, and I shall have a worshipper when thou art vanished." (: "The Eater of Souls," Henry Kuttner)

However, it also said that “Go therefore fearlessly, since god cannot conquer god, but only man who created him.” Simply put, it believes only humans who created god should be the ones to conquer god. (: "The Eater of Souls," Henry Kuttner)
